MINUTES of REGULAR MEETING
of the BOARD of COMMISSIONERS
of the CITY of BOWLING GREEN, KENTUCKY
held June 16, 2026

The Board of Commissioners of the City of Bowling Green, Kentucky met in regular session in
the Commission Chamber of City Hall, Bowling Green, Kentucky at 4:30 p.m. on June 16, 2026. Mayor
Todd Alcott called the meeting to order. Commissioner Carlos Bailey provided the invocation and all
present recited the Pledge of Allegiance. City Clerk Ashley Jackson called the roll, and the following
members were present: Commissioner Sue Parrigin, Commissioner Carlos Bailey, Commissioner Dana
Beasley-Brown, Commissioner Melinda Hill and Mayor Todd Alcott. Absent: none. There was a full
quorum of the Board of Commissioners.

CITY MANAGER

City Manager Jeffery B. Meisel requested the audience to sign up at the back of the Commission
Chamber to speak during public comments.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
Regular Meeting June 2, 2026.

Minutes of the above-referenced regular meeting were distributed to the Board of Commissioners
with the Agenda for review. Motion was made by Parrigin and seconded by Hill to approve said minutes.
Mayor Alcott asked for discussion, and with none, a roll call vote was taken.

ROLL CALL: Voting Yea: Parrigin, Bailey, Beasley-Brown, Hill and Alcott
Voting Nay: None
Minutes of the regular meeting of June 2, 2026 was approved by unanimous vote.
REGULAR AGENDA
MUNICIPAL ORDER NO. 2026 —135
MUNICIPAL ORDER APPROVING THE PROMOTION OF RANDAL
COCHRAN TO THE POSITION OF CREW SUPERVISOR II IN THE
. PARKS AND RECREATION DEPARTMENT

Summary of Municipal Order No. 2026 — 135 was read by the City Clerk. Motion was made by
Beasley-Brown and seconded by Bailey for consideration of said Municipal Order. Parks and Recreation
Director Brent Belcher reviewed and recommended the promotion of Randal Cochran to the position of
Crew Supervisor IT in the Parks and Recreation Department. Mayor Alcott asked for additional discussion,
and with none, a roll call vote was taken.

ROLL CALL: Voting Yea: Parrigin, Bailey, Beasley-Brown, Hill and Alcott
Voting Nay: None

Municipal Order No. 2026 — 135 was approved by unanimous vote.

MUNICIPAL ORDER NO. 2026 — 141
MUNICIPAL ORDER AUTHORIZING THE HOUSING AUTHORITY
OF BOWLING GREEN TO RETAIN THE CITY’S PORTION OF THE
PAYMENT IN LIEU OF TAXES (PILOT) FOR THE 2025 TAX YEAR
IN THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF $33,890.73
Summary of Municipal Order No. 2026 — 141 was read by the City Clerk. Motion was made by
Bailey and seconded by Hill for consideration of said Municipal Order. Meisel recommended approval
of the Housing Authority of Bowling Green to retain the City’s portion of the Payment in Lieu of Taxes
(PILOT) for the 2025 tax year in the amount of $33,890.73. The funds would be used for the after-school
program. Mayor Alcott asked for additional discussion, and with none, a roll call vote was taken.

ORDINANCE NO. BG2026 — 6
(Second Reading — Binding)
ORDINANCE AMENDING ZONING ORDINANCE
ORDINANCE AMENDING ARTICLES 3, 4, 5, 8 AND ADDING
APPENDIX C OF THE ZONING ORDINANCE FOR THE CITY OF
BOWLING GREEN, KENTUCKY AS RECOMMENDED BY THE
CITY-COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION

Title and summary of Ordinance No. BG2026 — 6 was read by the City Clerk. Motion was made
by Hill and seconded by Parrigin for the second and binding reading of said Ordinance. Mayor Alcott
explained everyone wanting to speak would need to sign up, and he would be calling individuals up to the
podium one at a time. At the request of the Mayor, City-County Planning Commission Executive Director
Ben Peterson reviewed the data center restrictions that were included in the Zoning Ordinance and
explained no current property was available that didn’t require a public hearing by the City-County
Planning Commission and would require meeting specific use standards. Additionally, Bowling Green
Area Chamber of Commerce Interim CEO/President Meredith Wilson made remarks on how the Chamber
of Commerce, City and County were taking proactive measures to establish zoning restrictions and
clarified that no data center was pursuing the area at this time. Thirty-three (33) individuals spoke in
opposition of data centers coming to the community and/or encouraged a moratorium. The main concerns
voiced were related to the negative impacts data centers would have on taxpayers and properties, as well
as pollution, noise and infrastructure. One additional comment was from an individual thanking city
leadership for the proactive approach and expressed support for the ordinance. The Board of
Commissioners made remarks and questions were answered.

Commissioner Dana Beasley-Brown requested to add a late-file item to the agenda. Motion was
made by Beasley-Brown and seconded by Bailey to add Municipal Order No. 2026 — 158 to the agenda.
Mayor Alcott asked for additional discussion, and with none, a roll call vote was taken.

ROLL CALL: Voting Yea: Parrigin, Bailey, Beasley-Brown and Hill
Voting Nay: Alcott
Motion to add Municipal Order No. 2026 — 158 to the agenda for consideration was approved by
majority vote.
LATE-FILE
MUNICIPAL ORDER NO. 2026 — 158
MUNICIPAL ORDER CREATING A DUE DILIGENCE PERIOD OF
SIX (6) MONTHS ON DATA CENTER APPLICATIONS, ZONING
10

(Minutes-Board of Commissioners-June 16, 2026)
AMENDMENTS AND/OR PERMITS, CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS,
BUILDING PERMITS, SITE PLANS, BUSINESS REGISTRATIONS
AND ANY OTHER REQUESTS RELATED TO THE LOCATION OF
DATA CENTERS IN THE CITY OF BOWLING GREEN
Summary of Municipal Order No. 2026 — 158 was read by the City Clerk. Commissioner Beasley-
Brown explained she proposed a six (6) month due diligence to allow additional time to address noise
concerns and host more work sessions, and Commissioner Bailey expressed his support for a due diligence
period. Following some additional comments, a roll call vote was taken.
ROLL CALL: Voting Yea: Bailey and Beasley-Brown
Voting Nay: Hill, Parrigin and Alcott
Municipal Order No. 2026 — 158 failed for a lack of majority vote.
Once all discussion concluded, a roll call vote was taken for Ordinance No. BG2026 — 6.
ROLL CALL: Voting Yea: Parrigin, Bailey, Beasley-Brown, Hill and Alcott
Voting Nay: None
Ordinance No. BG2026 — 6 was adopted by unanimous vote.
ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business to come before the Board of Commissioners, at approximately
9:00 p.m., Mayor Alcott declared this meeting adjourned.
